blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Tribunals were incorporated into the Constitution under Part XIV-A by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976.
Article 323A enables Parliament to establish Administrative Tribunals for public service disputes, leading to the establishment of the CAT in 1985.
Article 323B deals with tribunals for other specialized matters such as taxation, land reforms, industrial disputes, and corporate issues.
In the L. Chandra Kumar Case (1997), the Supreme Court restored judicial review, making tribunal decisions appealable before High Courts.
The Tribunal Reforms Act, 2021 introduced uniform service tenures and rationalized the number of existing tribunals.

blocks.content: Tribunals are quasi-judicial bodies established to deal with specific types of disputes. They were created to reduce the burden on regular courts and to provide speedy justice in specialized matters.
Tribunals perform judicial as well as administrative functions and work under the supervision of the judiciary.

Article 323A empowers Parliament to establish Administrative Tribunals for:

items:
• Service matters of central government employees
  • Disputes relating to recruitment and service conditions

blocks.content: Under this article, the Central Administrative Tribunal (CAT) was established in 1985.
The CAT deals with service matters of:

items:
• Central Government employees
  • Employees of Union Territories
  • Employees of public sector undertakings

• Headed by a Chairman
  • Benches across India
  • Decisions are subject to judicial review by High Court
Decisions are subject to judicial review by High Court

blocks.content: State Governments can establish State Administrative Tribunals for their employees. Features:

items:
• Created with approval of Parliament
  • Can be abolished later
  • Decisions are appealable in High Court
Decisions are appealable in High Court

blocks.content: Tribunals play a vital role in:

items:
• Speedy justice delivery
  • Reducing pendency of courts
  • Specialized dispute resolution
Article 323A tribunals can be established ONLY by Parliament, whereas Article 323B tribunals can be established by both Parliament and State Legislatures within their legislative competence.
Decisions of tribunals are NOT directly appealable to the Supreme Court; post L. Chandra Kumar (1997), an aggrieved party must first approach the concerned High Court.
CAT was established in 1985 under the Administrative Tribunals Act passed pursuant to Article 323A.

blocks.content: Tribunals are an essential part of the Indian judicial system. They provide speedy and expert justice in specialized matters.
However, proper reforms and independence are necessary to ensure their effective functioning.
